name: Alamūt Castle and Related Fortifications
description: Alamūt, whose name means "Eagle's Nest", is a ruined mountain fortress in the Alborz range of Qazvin Province, about 200 km from Tehran. From 1090 it was the headquarters of the Nezāri Ismaʿilis, who linked it with six other strongholds. It was fabled for its gardens and library, until the Mongols dismantled it in 1256.
